## What's new in 0.29

0.29 is the biggest update the script has had. It now knows which game you're installing for, and it can change that game's own settings for you.

### A game database behind the script

- A community-maintained game database now drives the script. Each supported game has a profile with the EAX versions it supports, notes for each store, suggested community patches and links to sources.
- The script can scan your Steam and Heroic libraries and list the supported games you have installed, sorted by name and labelled with their store. A long list is split into pages that fit your terminal.
- Picking a game shows its profile before anything is installed. If a game can't get EAX back on Linux, for example because a patch removed it, the script says so and stops, or points you to a known workaround such as a Steam beta branch.
- Profiles are marked Tested or Untested, and only tested ones are shown unless you set `EAX_RESTORE_UNTESTED=1`.
- The database downloads only when it has changed, and you can search every profile from Browse game profiles in the Tools menu.

### The script changes the game's own settings

- A new Game Settings step turns on EAX and the right audio options in the game's config files or the Wine registry, so you don't have to find them in the game's menus. It can edit many kinds of config file, from plain ini files to binary files and the registry.
- You pick settings from a tick list. Each one shows the file, section and value it changes, and nothing is applied until you confirm. Settings that couldn't be applied are listed at the end.
- If a config file doesn't exist yet, the script asks you to launch the game once and then checks again.
- Uninstall puts every changed value back.

### Speakers and headphones

- Choose stereo speakers, headphones or surround once, from an arrow-key list. The script writes the matching setup to OpenAL Soft's `alsoft.ini` and, if the game has a speaker setting of its own, to the game as well.

### A clearer install

- The install runs in four phases. It starts with an overview, recaps your answers before anything changes, and shows progress bars for the downloads and the deploy.
- You can pick Stable or Latest builds of DSOAL and OpenAL Soft, and the script downloads only the ones you choose. It now uses kcat's DSOAL and OpenAL Soft only; the community DSOAL builds and the bundled HRTF pack were dropped.
- The audio API scan lists the files it found, matches DLL names in any case and finds COM DirectSound. If it can't decide, you choose DirectSound3D or OpenAL yourself, and you can override what it detected.
- OpenAL games without a profile are detected too, and their `OpenAL32.dll` is backed up and replaced.
- When a game folder mixes 32-bit and 64-bit executables, the script uses the more common one and tells you.
- You choose where the DLL override goes: the launcher's settings or the Wine prefix's registry. If Steam or Heroic is open, the script offers to close it and reopen it afterwards.
- The script backs up existing files without asking.
- Games that need Creative's `eax.dll` now get Creative's own EAX Unified installer instead of placeholder files.
- The VC++ runtime has its own step. It's repaired when Windows thinks it's installed but a DLL was replaced, and uninstall removes it completely.

### Heroic and Wine prefixes

- Heroic games run with the game's own Wine version. For games added to Heroic by hand, the script finds the real prefix, and games with no prefix of their own use Heroic's shared one.
- The script asks you to confirm the Steam prefix before using it, and runs protontricks against the game's own Steam install, Flatpak included.

### Menus and Tools

- A lettered main menu replaces the old install or uninstall question.
- The Tools menu lets you change a game's settings or speaker setup later, turn DSOAL and OpenAL Soft logging on or off, install the VC++ runtime or EAX Unified into a prefix, and browse game profiles, all without a full reinstall.
- Uninstall lists the games you installed with the script by name and store, and asks what to remove.

### Other improvements

- At start-up the script checks for a newer version and offers to update itself.
- Every run is logged to `~/.local/state/eax-restore-linux/logs`, ready to attach to a bug report.
- There are `--help` and `--version` flags, and environment variables for scripting it, such as `EAX_RESTORE_ANSWERS_FILE` to answer the prompts from a file. The docs list them all.
- The script checks for read-only and case-insensitive (NTFS) drives before it writes anything.
- The desktop launcher keeps its window open until you press Enter.
- Messages are in plain language now, warnings are gathered in a recap at the end, and paths in your home folder show as `~/`.

### Fixes

- Yes/no prompts no longer read "no" as yes or "yes" as no.
- Typed paths with apostrophes work, and you can retype a path that's wrong.
- A deploy step that fails is no longer reported as done.
- The script exits instead of hanging when its input runs out.
- If kcat's latest DSOAL build isn't available, the script uses the archived one.
- Uninstalling a game installed with 0.28 removes its HRTF folder.

### For contributors

- The script is now built from separate source files in `src/`, with a bats test suite that runs in CI.
- `tools/profiler` is a browser-based editor and capture tool for writing game profiles and sending them in as pull requests.

`main` is now the stable branch and releases come from it. New work happens on `dev`, which publishes a pre-release build.
